title: Self-supervised learning identifies two previously unreported seismic sequences during the Mayotte submarine eruption
summary: A SimSiam self-supervised representation model with t-SNE and DBSCAN clustering explored two months of continuous seismological records from near the Fani Maoré submarine volcano. Researchers identified two previously undocumented multi-day sequences in October–November 2019, each beginning with increased volcano-tectonic events and followed by tremor-like, hydroacoustic or mixed signals. The paper describes the sequences as potentially associated with ongoing eruptive activity.
ai_technology: SimSiam self-supervised learning with t-SNE dimensionality reduction and DBSCAN clustering
organization: University of Strasbourg; Institut de Physique du Globe de Paris; NORSAR; University of Haute-Alsace; IFREMER

evidence.tested: A SimSiam self-supervised representation model with t-SNE and DBSCAN clustering explored two months of continuous seismological records from near the Fani Maoré submarine volcano.
evidence.unknown: The event data are from two months in 2019 and a nearby ocean-bottom seismometer; the study does not establish exact event locations or independently prove that each sequence was eruptive. Authors state that instrumental noise cannot be ruled out for some high-energy signals, and describe the volcanic association as potential. It is a peer-reviewed 2025 issue paper published online 2024-10-10.
evidence.ai_role: The self-supervised model constructed signal representations from full continuous seismograms; clustering surfaced two coherent, previously undocumented temporal event sequences that the researchers then interpreted using expert signal review. This avoids treating the result as a detector-only tool release.
